## Definitions

- [statement] Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI is an emerging candidate biomarker, but the strong performance of a small retrospective 7T study does not establish its accuracy in premotor, equivocal or atypical cases: its authors explicitly called for studies in those populations. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-024-00631-3 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET

## Structure and components

- [statement] MDS-UPDRS assesses four domains: Part I non-motor experiences of daily living, Part II motor experiences of daily living, Part III motor examination, and Part IV motor complications; it is used in clinical care and research. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19025984/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS · also: https://www.movementdisorders.org/MDS/MDS-Rating-Scales/MDS-Unified-Parkinsons-Disease-Rating-Scale-MDS-UPDRS.htm
- [statement] The original MDS-UPDRS clinimetric study tested 877 patients at 39 sites and found internal consistency of 0.79–0.93 across parts; factor analyses supported separate part sum scores in preference to an all-parts total. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19025984/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] An independent Spanish-language validation in 435 patients reported intraclass correlation above 0.85 for each part total, while noting a moderate floor effect (30 %) for Part IV. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22865238/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] Part III examination instructions require recording medication status, time since the last levodopa dose, and clinical ON/OFF state; these conditions matter when interpreting repeated motor examinations. (medium confidence) — https://www.movementdisorders.org/MDS-Files1/PDFs/Rating-Scales/MDS-UPDRS_English_FINAL.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6851993/
- [statement] In a study of the MDS-UPDRS Motor Examination (Part III) with 728 paired investigations of 260 patients, minimal clinically important difference estimates were asymmetric: −3.25 points for minimal clinically pertinent improvement and +4.63 for worsening, using clinician global-impression anchors and distribution methods. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26578041/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] A 2017 study of paired investigations from 365 patients estimated minimal meaningful changes in Part I of more than 2.64 points improvement or 2.45 worsening, and Part II of 3.05 improvement or 2.51 deterioration; these are study estimates for the specified parts. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28218413/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] Original UPDRS and MDS-UPDRS scores should not be treated as interchangeable: a 2012 calibration study supported conversion formulas for Parts II and III, but did not achieve concordance for Parts I and IV. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22886777/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] The MDS Non-Motor Rating Scale (MDS-NMS) consists of 13 domains plus a subscale for non-motor fluctuations and is rater-administered; in its initial multicenter validation study, internal consistency was acceptable (average Cronbach's alpha 0.66 and 0.84 for the scale total and the non-motor fluctuations total), interrater reliability was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient >0.95) and test-retest intraclass correlation was 0.84 for the scale total. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31571279/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] SynNeurGe links its biological components to a clinical component C, defined by either a single high-specificity feature or multiple lower-specificity clinical features. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38267191/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe

## How it works

- [statement] A critical review concluded that epidemiology alone makes causal attribution difficult because relevant exposures may precede manifest PD by decades; complementary experimental evidence increases causal plausibility. Observational associations should retain this qualification. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11832802/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] Pathogenic SNCA variants cause rare autosomal dominant PD; point mutations and gene multiplications are relevant variant classes. SNCA penetrance and phenotype depend on the variant. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/
- [statement] Conventional structural MRI identifies vascular damage, masses and patterns of atrophy that can cause or help distinguish parkinsonism; ordinary anatomical sequences have limited ability to identify the dopaminergic deficit itself. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6280219/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/
- [statement] The 2015 MDS criteria first require motor parkinsonism: bradykinesia together with rest tremor, rigidity, or both. Parkinsonism alone does not establish PD as its cause. (medium confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12748991/
- [statement] NICE NG71 recommends prompt, untreated referral to a specialist in differential diagnosis when PD is suspected, and regular diagnostic review at six- to twelve-month intervals with reconsideration if atypical features develop. Its diagnostic recommendation explicitly names the UK Brain Bank criteria. (low confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] A blinded comparison of three independent laboratories using PPMI CSF samples reported sensitivities of 86–96% and specificities of 93–100%, demonstrating reproducibility in expert laboratories despite methodological differences. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8572469/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] The 2025 biomatrix meta-analysis reported pooled blood SAA sensitivity of 0.90 (95% CI 0.86–0.93) and specificity of 0.91 (0.86–0.95); these pooled estimates are limited by aggregate data, publication bias and heterogeneous studies, and do not establish a universal blood-test performance. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12192484/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] In an analysis of PPMI and Tübingen cohort data, baseline SAA time-to-threshold predicted cognitive decline in both PPMI (hazard ratio 2·36, 95% CI 1·60–3·46) and Tübingen (2·17, 1·07–4·41), and was associated with cognitive decline in an Alzheimer-biomarker-negative PPMI subgroup. This was an observational prognostic association. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40541208/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] A 2025 modelling study using GBD 2021 projected 25.2 million people with PD worldwide in 2050 (95% uncertainty interval 21.7–30.1 million), a 112% increase from 2021; these are forecasts, not observed future counts. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-03-05) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11881235/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] The paraquat evidence has conflicting interpretations: Tanner and colleagues’ 2011 Agricultural Health Study nested case-control analysis reported an association with PD (OR 2.5, 95% CI 1.4–4.7); EPA’s page updated November 3, 2026 states that it has not found a clear link between labeled paraquat uses and PD. The regulatory statement is qualified by labeled-use conditions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-03) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3114824/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution · also: https://www.epa.gov/ingredients-used-pesticide-products/paraquat-dichloride
- [statement] A paraquat systematic review and meta-analysis (databases searched up to May 2019) found, across nine case-control studies, that PD occurrence was 25% higher in participants exposed to paraquat, while the only cohort investigation included showed a non-significant OR of 1.08; the authors concluded that the data indicate a positive association but that the weight-of-evidence does not enable one to assume an indisputable cause-effect relationship. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31476981/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] Tanner et al. reported an association between paraquat use and PD in FAME (110 cases, 358 controls; OR 2.5, 95% CI 1.4–4.7), whereas the later AHS prospective analysis reported no statistically clear association (HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.84–1.41). These overlapping study populations and different designs should not be counted as independent replications. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3114824/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7822498/
- [statement] In the 2014 swallow-tail MRI study, retrospective-cohort diagnostic accuracy was 96% on diagnostic scans and fell to 91% when non-diagnostic scans were included; scan quality therefore materially affected the reported performance. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3977922/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] A 2024 retrospective 7T neuromelanin MRI study included 21 PD patients, 13 essential-tremor patients and 18 controls; substantia nigra pars compacta total volume distinguished PD from the pooled non-PD group with reported sensitivity 100% and specificity 96.8%. These are within-study results. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-024-00631-3 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] In the 2018 eight-centre validation cohort of 626 patients, probable MDS PD had 94.5% sensitivity, 88.5% specificity and 92.6% overall accuracy against expert clinical diagnosis. These estimates measure agreement with expert clinical diagnosis, not autopsy confirmation. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30145797/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] A 2024 Mayo Clinic retrospective study matched 186 women and 186 men with iRBD; 48 patients (12.9%) phenoconverted during median follow-up of 6.0 years. Only age at diagnosis remained associated with conversion in the adjusted model (HR 1.09, 95% CI 1.06–1.13); the unadjusted association with antidepressant use must not be interpreted as evidence of neuroprotection. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11515114/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Prodromal PD: RBD, hyposmia and risk prediction

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] NfL interpretation needs covariate adjustment: the head-to-head study found associations with age in both CSF and plasma, and with body mass index, estimated glomerular filtration rate and chronic kidney disease in plasma. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12037818/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] The FDA’s August 19, 2024 Letter of Support recommends CSF SAA as a susceptibility/risk biomarker for trial enrichment and supports binary SAA assessment for selection into trials targeting common synuclein biology; its stated context is drug development and clinical trials. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-08-19) — https://www.fda.gov/media/181368/download · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] A Viewpoint cautions against premature adoption of the alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay as a Parkinson disease biomarker test in general neurology practice; this is an attributed clinical-implementation caution. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39102226/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] Neurofilament light chain can be measured in CSF and plasma as a marker of axonal damage; higher levels have been associated with poorer cognitive outcomes in Parkinson disease, but it is nonspecific and also rises with age and other inflammatory or degenerative conditions. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11226684/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] A 2019 PPMI analysis of 423 de novo patients estimated within-subject reliability of one-year change scores: Part II and Part III OFF each reached 0.50. Its authors cautioned that change scores contained substantial error variance. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6851993/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] Early-disease sensitivity requires caution: a Rasch analysis found floor effects and disordered response thresholds in Parts II and III; a separate comparison did not support greater sensitivity of MDS-UPDRS than UPDRS for mild motor severity in de novo PD. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6647182/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS · also: https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mdc3.13329
- [statement] The MDS website describes the MDS-UPDRS as a revision of the original Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (developed in the 1980s) that addresses problematic areas of the original scale identified by an MDS review task force; it was developed to evaluate non-motor and motor experiences of daily living and motor complications, includes a motor evaluation, and can be used in clinical settings and in research. (low confidence) — https://www.movementdisorders.org/MDS/MDS-Rating-Scales/MDS-Unified-Parkinsons-Disease-Rating-Scale-MDS-UPDRS.htm · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] The PDQ-39 is a short 39-item quality-of-life questionnaire for Parkinson's disease whose data can be presented in profile form or as a single index; a briefer derived measure (PDQ-8) also exists. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9617716/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] The Camp Lejeune result cannot uniquely attribute the association to TCE: exposure was inferred from residence, diagnostic data were limited to VHA/Medicare users, and PCE, vinyl chloride, benzene or mixtures could have contributed. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10186205/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] Air-pollution findings differ across settings: a Taiwan nationwide study reported positive associations for several pollutants that persisted in multipollutant models, while a Northern Ireland study found no overall association for medium-term PM₂.₅ or NO2 exposure and medication-defined PD onset; its under-50 subgroup showed a PM₂.₅ association. These exposure windows and outcome definitions limit direct comparison. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12322442/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12521372/
- [statement] The same Global Burden of Disease analysis reported male-to-female ratios of age-standardised prevalence rates of 1·40 (95% UI 1·36-1·43) in 2016 and 1·37 (1·34-1·40) in 1990, and estimated 211 296 deaths (95% UI 167 771-265 160) due to Parkinson's disease in 2016. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30287051/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] The Global Burden of Disease investigators concluded that the global burden of Parkinson's disease more than doubled over the past generation as a result of increasing numbers of older people, with potential contributions from longer disease duration and environmental factors. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30287051/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] A 2023 narrative review in J Parkinsons Dis (Dorsey and colleagues) reports that trichloroethylene (TCE) was first linked to parkinsonism in 1969, that four case studies involving eight individuals have linked occupational exposure to TCE to PD, and that a small epidemiological study associated occupational or hobby exposure with a 500% increased risk; the authors postulate that TCE contributes to the global rise of PD and state that further research is necessary to examine this hypothesis. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10041423/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] Pathogenic LRRK2 variants cause autosomal dominant PD with reduced, age-dependent penetrance; inheriting a pathogenic variant does not guarantee disease. (medium confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4501942/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/
- [statement] Marder and colleagues (2015) estimated PD risk to age 80 at 0.26 (95% CI 0.18–0.36) in relatives predicted to carry LRRK2 G2019S in an Ashkenazi Jewish kin-cohort. This is an ancestry- and ascertainment-specific estimate, not universal penetrance for every LRRK2 variant. - [statement] PRKN- and PINK1-related PD have autosomal recessive inheritance and are especially relevant in early-onset disease; established recessive disease must be distinguished from finding a single heterozygous variant. (medium confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/
- [statement] GeneReviews describes PRKN-related PD as usually beginning before age 35 with slow progression and relatively milder non-motor manifestations; PINK1-related PD has a similar phenotype, with psychiatric features more prominent. - [statement] Large studies have not demonstrated increased PD risk from a single heterozygous pathogenic PRKN variant. The UK Biobank/NIH-PD study found similar PD likelihood in single-variant carriers and noncarriers; this does not establish recessive PRKN disease in a monoallelic carrier. (medium confidence) — https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/publications/heterozygous-prkn-mutations-are-common-but-do-not-increase-the-risk-of-parkinsons-disease/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/
- [statement] In the 2024 PD GENEration publication, 8301 participants had received results from enrollment through June 2023; 13% had reportable variants and 9.1% of those without the specified high-risk factors had reportable variants. Reportable included pathogenic, likely pathogenic and risk variants, so the yield is not a count of confirmed monogenic diagnoses. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39074992/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] GBA1 encodes the lysosomal enzyme glucocerebrosidase. Biallelic disease-causing variants are associated with Gaucher disease, whereas heterozygous variants can increase PD risk; these are different genetic counseling contexts. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12162886/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] GeneReviews explicitly describes disagreement about classifying GBA1-associated PD as monogenic disease or a risk-factor association, while noting that some Gaucher-causing variants have higher penetrance. The classification should be qualified by variant and population. - [statement] Heterozygous GBA1 variants increase PD risk with variable penetrance, whereas biallelic Gaucher-disease-causing GBA1 variants are associated with Gaucher disease. - [statement] GBA1-associated PD risk depends on variant severity and genetic background; the UK Biobank/LuxPark study found that polygenic risk modified risk among carriers, so a single penetrance estimate should not be applied to every carrier. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12162886/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/
- [statement] A meta-analysis of 17 datasets from Parkinson's disease genome-wide association studies in European ancestry samples identified 90 independent genome-wide significant risk signals across 78 genomic regions; these 90 variants explained 16-36% of the heritable risk of Parkinson's disease depending on prevalence. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31701892/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] Presynaptic dopamine-transporter imaging supports distinguishing essential tremor from neurodegenerative parkinsonism; an abnormal DaTscan is not specific for idiopathic Parkinson’s disease and cannot reliably separate it from atypical degenerative parkinsonism.
