- [statement] Conventional structural MRI generally does not confirm PD, but can identify alternative structural causes or findings suggesting atypical parkinsonism; its sensitivity for atypical syndromes is limited early in disease. (medium confidence) — https://www.apdaparkinson.org/article/what-is-a-datscan-and-should-i-get-one/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/58/12/1888
- [statement] FDG-PET measures regional cerebral glucose metabolism and can support differentiating parkinsonian syndromes using disease-associated patterns; this is a different biological readout from presynaptic dopamine-terminal imaging. (medium confidence) — https://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/58/12/1888 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10423182/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6280219/, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10072-022-06166-w, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/
- [statement] The EANM/SNMMI guideline describes fluorodopa PET as a presynaptic dopaminergic assessment and notes that atypical parkinsonian syndromes usually cannot be separated from idiopathic PD with this technique; FDG-PET instead evaluates metabolic patterns. PET tracers should therefore not be treated as interchangeable tests. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/58/12/1888
- [statement] PET measures depend on the tracer: fluorodopa uptake reflects tracer influx and decarboxylation in presynaptic dopamine assessment, whereas FDG-PET maps regional glucose metabolism and disease-related metabolic patterns. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6280219/
- [statement] The EANM/SNMMI guideline warns that DAT binding reaches a floor later in disease, weakening its correlation with further clinical progression; scan signal should not be treated as a universally linear progression measure. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] The DATSCAN label (revised 11/2022) states that its effectiveness as a screening or confirmatory test, and for monitoring disease progression or response to therapy, has not been established. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] In the DATSCAN label's two multicenter studies of 284 adult patients with suspected parkinsonian syndromes, the clinical reference category parkinsonian syndromes (PS) comprised Parkinson's disease, multiple system atrophy and progressive supranuclear palsy, and the label states that DATSCAN imaging was not designed to distinguish among these conditions. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] NICE guideline NG71 (published 19 July 2017) recommends considering 123I‑FP‑CIT SPECT for people with tremor if essential tremor cannot be clinically differentiated from parkinsonism, and says not to use PET in the differential diagnosis of parkinsonian syndromes except in the context of clinical trials. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] NICE guideline NG71 (published 19 July 2017) says not to use structural MRI to diagnose Parkinson's disease, while structural MRI may be considered in the differential diagnosis of other parkinsonian syndromes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] MDS red flags have explicit timing and severity: wheelchair-requiring gait progression within five years, severe autonomic failure within five years, and recurrent balance-related falls within three years; bilateral symmetric onset is another red flag. Confounding explanations and timing must be considered. (low confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] The 2015 MDS criteria were designed to codify expert clinical diagnosis for research and can guide clinical assessment; diagnostic accuracy varies with disease duration and examiner expertise, so criteria performance should not be treated as one universal accuracy number. (medium confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30145797/
- [statement] A predominantly lower-limb gait syndrome can suggest vascular parkinsonism, but cerebrovascular imaging abnormalities are not conclusive because vascular disease and PD may coexist. Normal-pressure hydrocephalus is another potentially treatable mimic with gait, urinary and cognitive symptoms and ventriculomegaly. (low confidence) — https://exonpublications.com/index.php/exon/article/view/191/349 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] The UK Parkinson’s Disease Society Brain Bank criteria, reproduced from Gibb and Lees (1988), first define a parkinsonian syndrome as bradykinesia plus at least one of muscular rigidity, 4–6 Hz rest tremor, or postural instability not caused by primary visual, vestibular, cerebellar or proprioceptive dysfunction (step 1); step 2 lists exclusion criteria for Parkinson’s disease, including supranuclear gaze palsy, cerebellar signs, early severe autonomic involvement and neuroleptic treatment at onset of symptoms. (low confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK379754/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Step 3 of the UK Parkinson’s Disease Society Brain Bank criteria lists supportive prospective positive criteria, three or more of which are required for diagnosis of definite Parkinson’s disease: unilateral onset, rest tremor present, progressive disorder, persistent asymmetry affecting the side of onset most, excellent response (70–100%) to levodopa, severe levodopa-induced chorea, levodopa response for 5 years or more, and a clinical course of 10 years or more. (low confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK379754/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] The Movement Disorder Society task-force critique describes Hoehn–Yahr as nonlinear and heavily weighted toward postural instability, with incomplete coverage of other motor disability and no information on nonmotor problems. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15372591/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe
- [statement] In its report, the Movement Disorder Society task force recommended the original Hoehn–Yahr form for demographic group descriptions, reporting medians and ranges, and nonparametric analysis of changes; it reported no clinimetric data then available for the widely adopted half-stage modification. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15372591/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe
- [statement] Braak’s proposed pattern does not apply to every patient: the 2017 review limits its staging fit to a subset with young onset and long disease duration, while the 2008 critical evaluation reports exceptions and neurologically intact people with extensive postmortem pathology. (medium confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2017.00037/full · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/
- [statement] Höglinger and Lang explicitly distinguish SynNeurGe classification from staging: they refrained from proposing disease stages pending prospective evidence establishing temporal order; NSD-ISS is a separate staging proposal. (low confidence) — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1877718X241298194 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.alzforum.org/news/research-news/biological-definition-parkinsons-disease-two-proposals-pave-way
- [statement] In their 2024 comparison, Höglinger and Lang classify an isolated S-positive result without confirmed neurodegeneration as Parkinson’s/Lewy-type synucleinopathy, whereas they describe NSD-ISS as assigning such individuals stage 1A; they dispute treating this finding alone as a clinical disease diagnosis. (low confidence) — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1877718X241298194 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe
- [statement] The Braak pathological sequence is not universal across patients or Lewy-body disorders; reviews describe nonconforming distributions, so it should not be assumed to represent every patient’s disease course. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2017.00037/full
- [statement] Burke and colleagues cautioned that Braak pathological stages cannot be directly equated with clinical severity or inevitable future clinical Parkinson’s disease: their review describes advanced pathological stages in neurologically unimpaired individuals and no relationship with clinical severity in the data examined. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe
- [statement] SynNeurGe’s proposed biological classification has three components: pathological α-synuclein in tissues or CSF (S), imaging evidence of neurodegeneration (N), and pathogenic variants that cause or strongly predispose to Parkinson’s disease (G). (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38267191/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.alzforum.org/news/research-news/biological-definition-parkinsons-disease-two-proposals-pave-way
- [statement] Published interpretations differ: an autopsy-based study concluded that the PD staging scheme is valid except in the setting of advanced Alzheimer’s disease, whereas Burke and colleagues judged the evidence insufficient to establish the proposed caudal-to-rostral temporal progression of human Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20187227/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/
- [statement] In an analysis of PPMI, PASADENA and SPARK data published in npj Parkinson's Disease in 2024, 1741 participants had SAA data and 1030 (59%) were S+ consistent with neuronal alpha-synuclein disease (NSD); among sporadic PD, 683/736 (93%) were NSD, with a baseline distribution across NSD-ISS Stages 2B, 3 and 4 of 25%, 63% and 9%. The authors state that validation of the proposed anchors in longitudinal cohorts is necessary. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-024-00789-w · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe
- [statement] Isolated RBD involves dream enactment and loss of normal REM sleep atonia in the absence of an established neurodegenerative disorder. The cited risk cohorts used polysomnography-confirmed RBD; their estimates should not be assigned to questionnaire-positive dream enactment alone. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6391615/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Prodromal PD: RBD, hyposmia and risk prediction · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11515114/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11208573/
- [statement] Isolated RBD is a strong prodromal marker for a spectrum of neurodegenerative outcomes, including Parkinson’s disease, dementia with Lewy bodies and multiple system atrophy; a reported overall phenoconversion rate is therefore not a PD-only conversion rate. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6391615/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Prodromal PD: RBD, hyposmia and risk prediction · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11515114/
- [statement] A 2019 meta-analysis of seven prospective studies reported an association between hyposmia and subsequent PD, with pooled relative risk 3.84 (95% CI 2.12–6.95) across follow-up periods of 3–17 years. This relative risk is not an absolute probability that a person with hyposmia will develop PD. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6545790/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Prodromal PD: RBD, hyposmia and risk prediction
- [statement] RBD conversion estimates depend on population, age, endpoint definitions and ascertainment. The 2019 multicentre investigators warned that predictor hazard ratios should not be extrapolated to the general population, and the 2024 Mayo investigators called for population-based, polysomnography-confirmed cohorts to quantify community risk. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6391615/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Prodromal PD: RBD, hyposmia and risk prediction · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11515114/
- [statement] A negative baseline prodromal assessment cannot reliably rule out later phenoconversion in iRBD. In the 2019 cohort, even participants negative for the MDS prodromal criteria had conversion estimates of 5% at 3 years, 13% at 5 years and 27% at 8 years. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6391615/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Prodromal PD: RBD, hyposmia and risk prediction

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the 2023 cross-sectional PPMI study, CSF SAA sensitivity for clinically diagnosed Parkinson disease was 87·7% (95% CI 84·9–90·5) and specificity against healthy controls was 96·3% (93·4–99·2); these estimates describe that study population rather than general-population screening. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10627170/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] SAA positivity is heterogeneous: in the 2023 PPMI study, sensitivity in sporadic Parkinson disease with olfactory deficit was 98·6%, compared with 78·3% without olfactory deficit. A negative result therefore cannot universally exclude clinically diagnosed Parkinson disease. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10627170/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] NfL is a marker of neuroaxonal injury that can complement alpha-synuclein SAA, rather than directly measuring alpha-synuclein seeds. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12037818/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] In the 2025 head-to-head NfL study, CSF assays discriminated Parkinson’s disease from atypical parkinsonian disorders more accurately than plasma assays (AUC 0.966–0.974 versus 0.917–0.924); combining CSF NfL with alpha-synuclein RT-QuIC improved accuracy in that cohort. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12037818/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] The 2024 Zarkali review reports associations of baseline CSF Alzheimer-related biomarkers—higher phosphorylated tau, lower amyloid-beta 42, and lower amyloid-beta 42/total tau ratio—with worsening motor and cognitive performance at follow-up; these characterize co-pathology and prognosis rather than alpha-synuclein seeding itself. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11226684/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] In a blinded 30-site cross-sectional study, skin biopsy detected cutaneous phosphorylated alpha-synuclein in 92.7% (89 of 96) of patients with PD, 98.2% (54 of 55) with MSA, 96.0% (48 of 50) with DLB and 100% (22 of 22) with pure autonomic failure, versus 3.3% (4 of 120) of controls; the authors state that further research in unselected clinical populations is needed to externally validate the findings. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10955354/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] The Camp Lejeune cohort study found higher odds of PD among veterans stationed at the contaminated base than among Camp Pendleton veterans (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.39–2.07). Exposure concerned water containing TCE and other volatile organic compounds, rather than an isolated TCE exposure. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10186205/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] The critical review by Atterling Brolin and colleagues argues that converging epidemiological and experimental evidence supports stronger environmental policy action; this is the review authors’ assessment of causality and prevention, rather than proof that every exposure causes PD. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11832802/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] A UK paraquat-manufacturing workforce mortality study found no evidence of increased PD mortality (SMR 0.67, 95% CI 0.18–1.72). It assessed death-certificate outcomes rather than incident PD and disclosed Syngenta funding. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8157632/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] In the Global Burden of Disease analysis, 6·1 million (95% uncertainty interval 5·0-7·3) individuals had Parkinson's disease globally in 2016, compared with 2·5 million (2·0-3·0) in 1990; age-standardised prevalence rates increased by 21·7% (95% UI 18·1-25·3) over the same period. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30287051/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] In the 2025 UK Biobank/LuxPark study, severe and mild GBA1 variant groups had nearly double the PD risk of the risk-variant group, and polygenic background further stratified risk. These are cohort associations rather than a deterministic individual prediction. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12162886/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] In the EANM/SNMMI guideline, early idiopathic Parkinson’s disease typically shows reduced uptake first in the posterior putamen opposite the symptomatic side, with greater putaminal than caudate involvement; this is a typical pattern rather than a disease-specific signature. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] The EANM/SNMMI guideline interprets persistent scans without dopaminergic deficit as evidence against idiopathic PD; Palermo and colleagues instead reported eight older-onset levodopa-responsive cases with initially normal scans, two later abnormal. Their cases lacked pathological confirmation, so this is an attributed limitation rather than proof that normal scans commonly miss PD. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9092727/
- [statement] A 2023 retrospective clinical series of 156 patients referred for suspected atypical parkinsonism found overall FDG-PET classification accuracy of 74%, using follow-up clinical diagnosis rather than autopsy as the reference; the reader had access to prior dopamine-transporter imaging. The authors acknowledge reference-standard bias and missing histopathological confirmation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10423182/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] DaTscan uses iodine-123 ioflupane SPECT to visualize striatal dopamine transporter availability; it is an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations rather than a standalone disease identification test. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/
- [statement] For dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), the DATSCAN label reports, in 55 patients clinically diagnosed with DLB or Alzheimer's disease and compared with autopsy diagnosis, sensitivity of 80% (95% CI 61% to 92%) and specificity of 92% (95% CI 74% to 99%); the label derives this evidence from the scientific literature. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] A meta-analysis of nigrosome-1 appearance on MRI included nineteen studies with a total of 1508 participants (903 idiopathic PD patients and 605 healthy controls) and reported pooled sensitivity 0.94 (95 percent CI 0.93-0.96) and specificity 0.90 (95 percent CI 0.88-0.92) for differentiating idiopathic PD from healthy adults; the comparison was with healthy adults rather than other parkinsonian syndromes. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32668370/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] Asymmetric parkinsonism with higher cortical features such as apraxia, cortical sensory loss or alien-limb phenomena suggests corticobasal syndrome rather than typical PD. (low confidence) — https://exonpublications.com/index.php/exon/article/view/191/349 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Braak staging proposes a neuropathological sequence beginning in lower-brainstem or olfactory structures, proceeding toward substantia nigra involvement and eventually cortex; the proposed direction of spread is a hypothesis rather than a clinical disability score. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe · also: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2017.00037/full, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20187227/
- [statement] Braak’s six-pattern scheme inferred temporal progression from progressively broader postmortem distributions of abnormal α-synuclein staining; in that proposed sequence substantia-nigra involvement appears around stage 3, rather than at its earliest stage. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2605160/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD staging: Hoehn-Yahr, Braak and biological SynNeurGe
- [statement] The MDS research framework combines an age-based prior probability with marker likelihood ratios in a Bayesian naïve classifier; probable prodromal PD means at least 80% estimated certainty that prodromal disease is present, rather than an 80% prediction of clinical conversion within a specified number of years. (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26474317/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Prodromal PD: RBD, hyposmia and risk prediction · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11208573/
- [statement] Postuma and colleagues’ 2019 study followed 1280 polysomnography-confirmed iRBD patients from 24 centres: mean age was 66.3 years, 82.5% were men, and mean follow-up was 4.6 years. Overall conversion to an overt neurodegenerative syndrome was 6.3% per year, with Kaplan–Meier estimated conversion of 73.5% at 12 years; these are study estimates rather than universal individual prognoses. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6391615/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Prodromal PD: RBD, hyposmia and risk prediction
- [statement] The 2024 Lifelines analysis found poor discrimination (ROC-AUC 0.577) using a subset of MDS risk and prodromal markers in 160 self-reported PD converters and 320 matched controls. Only six of eleven risk markers and six of twelve prodromal markers could be inferred, so this result scopes a partial, largely questionnaire-based implementation rather than invalidating the complete criteria. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11208573/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Prodromal PD: RBD, hyposmia and risk prediction

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Alpha-synuclein SAA detects seeding-competent misfolded aggregates by amplifying their ability to template recombinant alpha-synuclein aggregation; thioflavin T fluorescence detects the resulting fibrils. RT-QuIC and PMCA are related SAA approaches. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8572469/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11226684/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12192484/
- [statement] Expert-laboratory concordance does not remove the need for assay standardization: protocol heterogeneity, recombinant substrate, buffers, beads, shaking, temperature, and preanalytical handling affect comparability. (high confidence) — https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/acn3.70384 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13347450/
- [statement] Blood alpha-synuclein assays require control of peripheral contamination and sample handling: erythrocytes and platelets contribute alpha-synuclein, and hemolysis and storage conditions can vary results. CSF SAA also requires preanalytical controls, including blood contamination and freeze-thaw handling. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12192484/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13347450/
- [statement] SAA seeding activity and total CSF alpha-synuclein concentration are different measurements: the 2024 Zarkali review found that total CSF alpha-synuclein did not show a consistent relationship with Lewy body pathology or longitudinal motor or cognitive change. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11226684/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] Longitudinal prognostic results differ by analysis: a PPMI analysis found no statistically significant association between baseline seeding measures and progression among manifest patients, whereas a separate analysis associated baseline time-to-threshold with subsequent cognitive decline in PPMI and an independent Tübingen cohort. Diagnostic positivity should not be treated as an established general progression measure. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12354789/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40541208/
- [statement] CSF sampling is relatively invasive, motivating SAA studies in other specimens. The 2024 Zarkali review describes promising skin-biopsy results and lower accuracy with olfactory-mucosa sampling; performance should be interpreted for the specimen and assay actually tested. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11226684/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] Goldman and colleagues’ discordant-twin study associated TCE exposure with PD (OR 6.1, 95 percent CI 1.2–33). The very wide interval makes the effect size imprecise. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3366287/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] Xie and colleagues’ 2025 meta-analysis estimated a pooled OR of 1.10 (95 percent CI 1.03–1.17) for PD with each 5 μg/m3 increase in long-term PM2.5 exposure. This is an observational pooled association. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11861764/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] The 2025 Northern Ireland cohort found no adjusted overall association between medium-term PM₂.₅ or NO2 exposure and medication-defined PD onset, but reported a positive PM₂.₅ association in participants under 50. Its findings therefore do not support a uniform association across age groups. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12521372/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] A nationwide Taiwan cohort reported positive associations between air-pollutant exposure and PD incidence that persisted in multipollutant models; this observational result does not establish a universal exposure effect. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12322442/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] In the same projection, population ageing was the largest contributor to the projected growth in cases, ahead of population growth and changes in prevalence. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11881235/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Epidemiology and environmental risk factors: paraquat, TCE, air pollution
- [statement] Heterozygous GBA1 variants increase PD susceptibility with variable penetrance influenced by age, variant and genetic background; a carrier result alone does not establish that PD will develop. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12162886/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/
- [statement] PD panels need attention to copy-number analysis: sequencing alone may miss deletions or duplications, particularly relevant to SNCA and PRKN. Check whether the assay includes deletion/duplication testing. (medium confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/
- [statement] GBA1 coverage differs among laboratories: verify inclusion and full sequencing. Expanded testing can identify variants of uncertain significance that require expert interpretation and may remain inconclusive. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] Genetic counseling should explain inheritance, penetrance and test limitations. Expert review supports pretest and posttest counseling; GeneReviews specifically recommends discussing limitations and consequences before predictive testing of asymptomatic relatives. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1 · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1223/
- [statement] Testing beyond selected known variants can reveal variants of uncertain significance requiring expert interpretation; such findings may not establish pathogenicity. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946878/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Genetics of PD: LRRK2, GBA1, SNCA, PRKN, PINK1
- [statement] DAT-SPECT interpretation requires checking potentially interfering drugs and structural imaging: cocaine, amphetamines and methylphenidate can markedly reduce tracer binding, while anatomic lesions and atrophy can alter apparent striatal binding or shape. Medication changes require clinician-directed preparation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] A 2014 primary MRI study showed that healthy nigrosome-1 can appear as a swallow-tail hyperintensity on high-resolution 3T susceptibility-weighted imaging, with this appearance lost in PD. The authors called for independent prospective validation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3977922/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] The 2024 7T MRI authors identify small sample size, retrospective design and inclusion of established PD as limitations, and call for studies in equivocal PD and atypical parkinsonism; their reported accuracy should not be assumed to generalize to routine diagnostic populations. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-024-00631-3 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] In the same 7T study, neuromelanin volume discriminated groups, whereas contrast ratio did not differ significantly between PD and non-PD groups; a result for one MRI metric should not be generalized to all neuromelanin measurements. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-024-00631-3 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] In a retrospective study of eighty-three clinically confirmed degenerative parkinsonian cases, voxel-based FDG-PET maps added diagnostic accuracy and confidence, particularly for less experienced readers; expert-reader improvement was mainly supported by hypometabolism maps. (low confidence) — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10072-022-06166-w · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] DAT-SPECT quantification requires attention to acquisition and processing: the EANM/SNMMI guideline cautions that specific binding ratios from different cameras, acquisition methods, processing and analyses are not directly interchangeable. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] The FDA prescribing information for DATSCAN (ioflupane I 123 injection), revised 11/2022, indicates it as an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations for striatal dopamine transporter visualization using single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) brain imaging in adult patients with suspected parkinsonian syndromes or suspected dementia with Lewy bodies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] MDS bradykinesia requires slowness plus decrement in amplitude or speed, or progressive hesitations/halts, during continued movement; limb bradykinesia must be documented. (low confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Clinically established PD under the 2015 MDS criteria requires no absolute exclusion, at least two supportive criteria, and no red flags. Clinically probable PD permits at most two red flags, each counterbalanced by a supportive criterion, with no absolute exclusion. (medium confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12748991/
- [statement] Supportive MDS features include a clear and dramatic dopaminergic treatment response, levodopa-induced dyskinesia, and clinically documented limb rest tremor; merely some improvement on treatment does not satisfy the dramatic-response criterion. (low confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Examples of 2015 MDS absolute exclusions are unequivocal cerebellar abnormalities, downward vertical supranuclear gaze palsy or selective slowing of downward saccades, and dopamine-blocking/depleting exposure whose dose and time course fit drug-induced parkinsonism. (low confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Essential tremor commonly produces bilateral postural/action tremor; PD can also have postural/action tremor, so tremor appearance alone is insufficient for diagnosis. (low confidence) — https://exonpublications.com/index.php/exon/article/view/191/349 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Medication review is central to differential diagnosis: drug-induced parkinsonism can be symmetric but can also closely mimic PD; symptoms often resolve after withdrawal, while continued progression can reflect underlying PD unmasked by the drug. (low confidence) — https://exonpublications.com/index.php/exon/article/view/191/349 · keywords: Parkinson's disease diagnosis and biomarkers: clinical criteria, prodromal stage, staging, genetics, alpha-synuclein seed amplification, imaging, epidemiology and rating scales, PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Early prominent autonomic problems, cerebellar signs or stridor raise suspicion of multiple system atrophy; early falls with vertical eye-movement abnormalities raise suspicion of progressive supranuclear palsy. These are differential clues, not guarantees of pathology. - [statement] Functional parkinsonism is assessed using positive examination signs such as effortful slowness without decrement, improvement with distraction, variable tremor, and active resistance during passive movement. - [statement] The autopsy-based scoping review by Fox and colleagues found that supportive features were more common in PD and exclusions/red flags more common in atypical disorders, but some atypical features also occurred in pathologically confirmed PD. Limited clinical documentation, retrospective application of precise definitions and co-pathology constrain interpretation. - [statement] SynNeurGe classifies pathological α-synuclein (S), neurodegeneration (N), and pathogenic genetic variants (G), linked to clinical manifestations (C); these are biological classification dimensions.
